purpose: Honors the DONOTCACHEPAGE constant across the static-HTML cache pipeline: the write path (Cache::is_not_cacheable/maybe_store_cache) refuses to store opted-out pages and writes a .wppo-no-cache filesystem marker that the generated advanced-cache.php drop-in checks before serving, plus a one-time version-upgrade routine that regenerates the drop-in and clears the full cache.
riskRationale: The core three-file fix is well-constructed and double-gated on the write path, but the commit ships ~4,700 dev-only vendor files (~525K lines) into the tracked vendor/ tree in violation of the production-only vendor convention, the serve path cannot stop serving an already-cached page that later sets DONOTCACHEPAGE (WordPress never boots to write the marker), the marker never self-heals so transiently/conditionally flagged URLs permanently lose static caching, and the version-gated migration cannot fire without a WPPO_VERSION bump.
breakingChanges: One-time full static cache clear and advanced-cache.php drop-in regeneration on first admin page load after a version change
URLs that ever trigger DONOTCACHEPAGE get a permanent .wppo-no-cache marker until a cache clear or post invalidation removes it
vendor/ now tracks dev-only dependencies instead of the production-only set

text: The dual write-path/serve-path design is sound: the write path is gated at the final storage decision in save_cache_files(), the drop-in marker check is a clean mirror with consistent path derivation (homepage, trailing slash, role variants), and the at-most-once guard prevents redundant I/O. However, the PR must not merge as-is: it commits the entire dev-dependency vendor tree contrary to AGENTS.md, the marker never self-heals (permanently disabling caching for URLs that only transiently set the constant), already-cached pages transitioning to DONOTCACHEPAGE keep being served stale because the drop-in serves before WordPress boots, the marker write can fail silently when the cache directory is absent, and the upgrade migration is a no-op for existing 1.8.0 installs unless WPPO_VERSION is bumped.

reasoning: The write-path gating and the serve-path marker are correct for pages never cached or rendered after the constant is set, but the dev vendor tree (~4,700 files) violates the production-only vendor policy, the marker lifecycle does not actually self-heal, the marker write silently fails when the parent cache directory is absent, and the version-gated migration cannot fire unless WPPO_VERSION is bumped in the same release. Several of these require design-level decisions or manual process steps rather than mechanical fixes, so an automated agent should not merge as-is.

message: Placing the DONOTCACHEPAGE gate in maybe_store_cache() as the final gate inside save_cache_files() correctly covers both the WP 6.9+ enhancement-buffer path and the legacy template_redirect path, catching constants defined mid-render after the earlier is_not_cacheable() checks already ran, while the 'html' === $type condition keeps CSS/JS minification unaffected.

The no_cache_marker_written property guarantees the marker write and stale-file purge run at most once per request even though is_not_cacheable() is reachable from multiple call sites (combine_css, start_output_buffer, process_buffer_for_cache, stash_cache), avoiding duplicate filesystem work.

The generated drop-in marker check is placed before any serve logic and keys off the page directory, so it also covers role-variant files; the marker path (dirname of the cached file) exactly matches the write-path marker including homepage and trailing-slash normalization, and the emitted code is lint-clean (php -l passes).

The marker lifecycle is integrated into the existing invalidation paths — single-page clear_cache(), invalidate_dynamic_static_html() smart purge, and the full recursive clear — so the marker's lifetime is consistent with every other cache artifact and caching can resume once the constant is no longer set.

The one-time version-upgrade routine is a sensible migration: it regenerates the drop-in via Advanced_Cache_Handler::create(), which still respects foreign drop-ins via foreign_dropin_present(), and clears the full cache once to purge stale pages the old drop-in would keep serving.

The commit adds ~4,700 files (~525K lines) of require-dev dependencies to the tracked vendor/ directory (phpunit, mockery, hamcrest, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, phpcompatibility, phpcsstandards, sebastian/*, nikic/php-parser, theseer/tokenizer, etc.) and regenerates the composer autoloader to reference them. AGENTS.md explicitly requires vendor/ to be production-only (run 'composer release' before committing), and the parent commit contained exactly the production packages (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler). The PR description only lists six vendor/composer files, understating the change, and .distignore excludes only a few of these paths, so the release ZIP would ship test/lint tooling.
suggestion: Run 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --ignore-platform-reqs), verify vendor/ no longer contains phpunit/mockery/phpcs/wpcs/brain/antecedent, and recommit the production-only vendor/ plus the regenerated composer autoload metadata. Consider a CI guard that fails when vendor/ contains require-dev packages.
suggestionCode:
composer release
# then git add vendor/ includes/ and commit only production deps

message: Residual stale-serve gap: the drop-in serves a cached index.html before WordPress boots, so for a page that is already cached when a plugin first sets DONOTCACHEPAGE, maybe_mark_page_not_cacheable() never runs and the marker is never written — the stale page keeps being served indefinitely until a cache clear, post save, or the one-time upgrade purge. This is exactly the issue #487 transition scenario, so the PR's claim that opted-out pages are 'never served from stale static files' is overstated.
suggestion: Document this as a best-effort limitation and scope the PR's guarantee to pages rendered at least once after the constant is set; optionally bound the stale window with a low-cost serve-path freshness check (e.g. skip serving when the cached file mtime is older than the option wppo_cache_last_cleared_time or a TTL).

message: The marker never self-heals: it is only removed by post-save invalidation, a single-page clear, or a full clear. A URL that sets DONOTCACHEPAGE only transiently/conditionally (campaign windows, time-of-day, per-session, membership or A/B conditions not tied to post saves) keeps its marker permanently, so the drop-in boots WordPress and re-renders the page on every request even after the constant stops being set — a silent, permanent caching loss that contradicts the PR's 'self-healing' claim.
suggestion: Delete the marker on the successful cacheable write path so caching resumes automatically once the constant is no longer set; the next request that actually sets DONOTCACHEPAGE re-creates the marker and purges stale files, so behavior converges safely.

message: maybe_run_version_upgrade() is hooked to admin_init with no capability check. admin_init fires for any authenticated user who can load any admin page (including subscribers) or POST to admin-ajax.php, so an unprivileged user can trigger a full cache wipe (Cache::clear_cache()) and advanced-cache.php regeneration on every version bump. Every other admin-triggered operation in this plugin (REST endpoints, admin notices, metabox) is gated on manage_options.
suggestion: Add a current_user_can('manage_options') guard as the first statement in maybe_run_version_upgrade() so only administrators can trigger the destructive upgrade routine.

message: maybe_mark_page_not_cacheable() writes the marker with put_contents() without ensuring the parent directory exists (WP_Filesystem_Direct::put_contents() does not create parent directories) and ignores the return value. On a DONOTCACHEPAGE URL that has never been cached (or whose directory was removed), the marker write silently fails and the serve-path protection never engages; the static html/gz files may already have been purged, so a later request without the constant can re-cache the page with no marker present.
suggestion: Create the cache directory before writing the marker (via $this->prepare_cache_dir()), skip the write when the marker already exists, and bail out/log when put_contents() returns false instead of silently no-op'ing.

message: The version-upgrade migration cannot fire: WPPO_VERSION is still '1.8.0' (performance-optimisation.php:37) while the new members are documented @since 1.9.0, so existing 1.8.0 installs compare equal and never regenerate the marker-aware drop-in or run the one-time full clear — the serve-path half of the fix is a silent no-op for them until a future release bumps the version. Separately, wppo_version is never set on activation, so fresh installs redundantly run the full upgrade routine (drop-in regen + cache clear) on their first admin load.
suggestion: Bump WPPO_VERSION in the same release and align the @since tags with the shipped version; set the wppo_version option during activation (class-activate.php) so fresh installs skip the redundant upgrade routine.

message: On every request to a page where DONOTCACHEPAGE is set, the marker is rewritten and the full stale-file purge (exists+delete checks plus a dirlist scan in delete_role_variant_files()) runs even when the marker already exists, adding unnecessary filesystem I/O to every dynamic render of high-traffic opted-out pages.
suggestion: Early-return when the marker already exists so the write and purge run at most once on disk.

message: The guard `if ( ! $this->maybe_store_cache() && 'html' === $type )` evaluates maybe_store_cache() for every file type because the left operand runs first, so the DONOTCACHEPAGE branch — which writes the marker and purges html/role files — can fire on a 'css' save. Unreachable today because combine_css() is already gated by is_not_cacheable(), but the operand order is fragile and the side effects are surprising.
suggestion: Reorder the guard so maybe_store_cache() only runs for html writes.

message: is_not_cacheable() is a predicate but now performs filesystem side effects (marker write + stale-file purge) via maybe_mark_page_not_cacheable(), and it is also used to gate CSS combining and buffer optimization, so the check/write coupling is surprising and hard to reason about despite the once-per-request guard.
suggestion: Separate the pure cacheability check from the side-effecting marker write (or rename the helper to reflect that it both evaluates and records the no-cache decision) so callers that only need to test cacheability do not touch the filesystem.

message: Pages that set DONOTCACHEPAGE but were not previously excluded now also skip output-buffer optimizations (next-gen image conversion, HTML minification, CDN rewrite) because is_not_cacheable() gates process_buffer_for_cache(), start_output_buffer(), and combine_css(). This matches how other non-cacheable pages behave, but it is a behavior change worth confirming is intended.
suggestion: If buffer optimizations should still apply to DONOTCACHEPAGE pages, gate the DONOTCACHEPAGE early-return to the cache-storage decisions (maybe_store_cache/stash_cache) rather than the shared is_not_cacheable() optimization gate.

message: maybe_run_version_upgrade() records wppo_version even when Advanced_Cache_Handler::create() fails (e.g. transient WP_Filesystem failure), so the marker-aware drop-in regeneration is never retried and pre-existing stale DONOTCACHEPAGE pages keep being served.
suggestion: Only update wppo_version when the drop-in is actually regenerated (or when a foreign drop-in was detected and create() correctly returned early); otherwise leave the option unchanged so a later admin_init retries the upgrade.

message: The upgrade routine is hooked to admin_init only, so sites updated via background auto-update or CLI (or whose admins do not visit wp-admin for a while) will not regenerate the marker-aware drop-in or clear stale DONOTCACHEPAGE pages until someone loads an admin page, silently delaying the fix for them.
suggestion: Also hook the one-time version check on 'upgrader_process_complete'/'activated_plugin', or run the version_compare on init since the option gate makes it one-time.

message: invalidate_dynamic_static_html() removes the .wppo-no-cache marker only for the edited post; the smart-purge blocks for the home page and posts/archives/terms (lines 903-944) delete their cache files but not their markers, so a home/archive page that had a marker stays uncached even after its content changes.
suggestion: Delete the marker alongside the cache files in the home, blog, archive, and term purge blocks, reusing the same delete_cache_files(dirname-relative '.wppo-no-cache') pattern used for the post itself.

message: No automated tests cover the new marker lifecycle (write-once guard, purge on single-page clear and post invalidation, version-upgrade drop-in regeneration), and the repo has no runnable PHP unit tests per AGENTS.md, so the highest-risk write/serve path interaction is shipped verified only by lint and manual checks.
suggestion: Add a PHP integration test or a documented manual test scenario covering: (1) a DONOTCACHEPAGE request writes the marker and purges existing html/gz/role variants, (2) clear_cache()/invalidate_dynamic_static_html() removes the marker, and (3) the generated drop-in returns early when the marker exists.
